title: The order in which custom element callbacks are called does not match implementations

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? > Elements are pushed onto the [backup element queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#backup-element-queue) during operations that affect the DOM without going through an API decorated with [[CEReactions]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#cereactions), or through the parser's [create an element for the token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) algorithm. An example of this is a user-initiated editing operation which modifies the descendants or attributes of an [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element. Code example: ```html hello ``` Here is the step-by-step logic: 1. The parser detects the initial token of the corresponding element and starts creating [an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) 2. Steps 8 and 11 are not executed, but step 9 is executed, which will create the element and it will have a [custom element state](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state) equal to "undefined", and step 10 won't [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction), since the [custom element state](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom-element-state) is not "custom". 3. To insert a node at the appropriate location in the DOM, the following operation will be performed for the created token element: [insert an element at the adjusted insertion location](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#insert-an-element-at-the-adjusted-insertion-location). Next, we will perform step 4, which says `"Insert element at the adjusted insertion location"`. Does this step relate to the [Insert](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert) algorithm from the DOM specification? Anyway if it is algorithm from the DOM specification, it doesn't enqueue any reaction into the [custom element reactions stack](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#custom-element-reactions-stack) 4. At the moment, we have no reactions associated with the currently created element, but as soon as the page parser encounters a script that has an API with an [element definition](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#element-definition) suitable for our element, step 19 occurs with [enqueue a custom element upgrade reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-upgrade-reaction) 5. Since the API with [element definition](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#element-definition) is decorated with [CEReactions], then upon its completion the [Invoke custom element reactions](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#invoke-custom-element-reactions) operation will occur (this call will occur when the [custom element reactions stack](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#custom-element-reactions-stack) is already empty) where there will be a single upgrade reaction. Of course, the reaction is called, it calls the [upgrade an element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#concept-upgrade-an-element) operation 6. While executing the current upgrade reaction, we encounter a constructor call, and also [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) for `"attributeChangedCallback"` and `"connectedCallback"`. The enqueue will happen for the [backup element queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#backup-element-queue) 7. The upgrade reaction call completes and the decorated [CEReactions] API call completes. 8. When the next microtask checkpoint occurs, we will have to perform our reactions for the element (and it would seem that here is proof that the [backup element queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#backup-element-queue) is used ). **But in fact, the same chrome does not do this and neither does firefox, and why?** If you run the code with the html above, you will notice that all the element lifecycle callbacks are executed before the very first microtask, which I scheduled before defining the custom element `customElements.define`. This is what both Chrome and Firefox show: - `constructor` - `attribute` - `connected` - `microtask 1` - `microtask 2` Although based on the step-by-step logic browsers should show the next: - `constructor` - `microtask 1` - `attribute` - `connected` - `microtask 2` But something is wrong here, I don't see this in Chrome or Firefox. Moreover, if you run Performance in Chrome and look at the graphs, you can clearly see that `"attributeChangedCallback"` and `"connectedCallback"` are launched in the script execution phase, and not as microtasks. What's the matter? --- What about this? > An example of this is a user-initiated editing operation which modifies the descendants or attributes of an [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element. To test this you need to do the following: 1. It is advisable to open a blank page so that third-party tasks on the graph do not interfere with your profiling 2. Enter in the Console tab `document.designMode = "on"`, and also paste the definition for the element (take it from the example in very beggining of page) 3. Copy the text from `a`, so that when you paste it into a document using `ctrl+v`, you notice that an element with text appears on the page, and not just text. 4. Run profiling on the Performance tab 5. Insert our element into the page using `ctrl+v` 6. Stop profiling and look at the graph This is what chrome gave me: Yes, there are those same microtasks (there are exactly 3 of them for each method), but how does the user agent parse the insertion? I did not notice that the specification somehow said how to act in such cases. Let's imagine that when inserting we use a parser, but the question is, which one exactly: [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#html-fragment-parsing-algorithm) or regular one? If we use the algorithm [create an element for the token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) then step 9 should perform [creating an element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element) , where the constructor for the element will be called, and this is not a microtask based on the operation. So [the create an element for the token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) algorithm is not suitable for inserting elements by the user? Referring to the image provided above, the first microtask in it is a constructor, that is, the user-initiated editing operation schedules the [create an element for the token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) as a microtask. Do I understand everything correctly? If so, what kind of parser is? Is it an [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#html-fragment-parsing-algorithm) or not? --- But there is one strange case if to the example above with user interaction we add an interesting listener ``` javascript window.addEventListener("textInput", () => {}) ``` then for some strange reason instead of the expected: - `constructor` - `attribute` - `connected` we will get: - `constructor` - `attribute` - `connected` - `attribute` How? No other listener except `textInput` does this. It seems that clearer wording is needed when using an API that is not decorated with [CEReactions], this case is an example. @domenic P.S I’m not yet sure which of what I described is a bug to create the appropriate issue on bugtracker. Thus, I will wait for an expert answer on this issue. --- If I'm wrong about something, I'll be glad to be wrong :)
